title: Normalize /v1/chat params for back-compat; add streaming heartbeat and tool-call envelope heuristics
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: several customers expect exact /v1/chat.completions parameter semantics (role aliases, stop array semantics, logprobs mapping) while also relying on our streaming runtime. This PR implements a compatibility-layer negotiator that accepts various OpenAI-like input shapes and normalizes them into Redwood's internal request model. It also introduces a lightweight stream-heartbeat packet and a tool-call envelope to make function/tool handshake deterministic under backpressure.

What this PR does (single-change summary): normalize incoming /v1/chat params (role/name aliases, stop normalization, n/stream flags, logprobs, top_p/temperature fallbacks), add a 2s stream-heartbeat frame for long-running responses, and wrap tool/function call payloads in a compact structured envelope so downstream SDKs can parse function metadata even when a stream is interrupted.

Key behaviors and compatibility notes:
- Roles: accepts both "role":"assistant" and older shape "system/assistant/human" aliasing; normalizer maps common typos (e.g., "user": "human", "assistant_bot": "assistant").
- Stop tokens: supports string or array input; when array, we preserve order and dedupe adjacent duplicates; empty-stop (null/[]) semantics preserved per user request.
- n / best_of: maps legacy best_of -> n with deterministic selection; ensures deterministic seed behavior when present.
- logprobs: maps OpenAI-style logprobs response to Redwood's token-level scoring. When model doesn't expose precise logprobs, we synthesize approximate buckets and annotate as "approx_logprobs" to avoid breaking consumers.
- tool/function calls: when a tool call is emitted, we send a structured envelope event: {"envelope_type":"tool_call","tool_name":...,"metadata":...} as a single JSON line frame to keep tool metadata separate from streaming text deltas. SDKs are updated in separate PRs to consume this.
- Stream heartbeat: emits an empty control frame every 2s (configurable via RD_STREAM_HEARTBEAT_MS) to keep HTTP/HTTP2 intermediaries from timing out on long generations. Heartbeats are filtered by client SDKs; they are not surfaced as content tokens.

Design decisions: keep normalization non-destructive — if a user passes an explicit param (e.g., temperature=0.0), we do not override. Only missing or ambiguous fields are mapped. The negotiator lives at the API adapter boundary to avoid polluting internal runtime types. The structured envelope uses a "frame_type" field so future frames can be introduced without protocol churn.

Testing: unit tests for param mapping, integration tests hitting a local runtime binary, and a new flaky-tolerant streaming test that validates heartbeat preservation through proxies. CI required two reruns due to a known flake in the macOS test matrix; both reruns passed.

Migration and rollout: feature is behind an API-compat feature flag (openai_v1_compat = true) and will be enabled for a subset of accounts first. No breaking changes expected. Docs update included (docs/openai_v1_chat.md) with explicit examples of role aliasing and tool-call envelope parsing.

Checklist:
- [x] Parameter normalizer implementation
- [x] Stream heartbeat implementation and runtime integration test
- [x] Tool-call envelope schema + SDK compatibility note
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Docs and migration notes

Notes: this PR intentionally favors defensive mapping to reduce customer breakages observed in support tickets. Follow-up PRs will add telemetry flags to measure how many requests rely on each mapping rule.
